The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that took place on 18.04.2022.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 18.04.2022 at about 9.00 a.m., when he was standing on the extreme left side to cross the road on Kunigal-Nelamangala N.H.-75 road, Narasandra, Kudur Hobli,
Magadi taluk, Ramangara, at that time, driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA- 13-P-3871 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner,
caused the accident and as a result, injured fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
It is contended that, immediately after the accident, injured was shifted to Magnus hospital wherein he took treatment for the accidental injuries.

It is stated that he has spent huge amount for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.
It is contended that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as agricultural coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able Mahesha N.B vs Manjunath K.H on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114224512/
2 to do his work as he was doing earlier and lost his income.
The accident in question was due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA- 13-P-3871.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. On service of notice, respondent No.1 and 2 have entered appearance through their learned counsels and the 2 nd respondent filed objection statement.
5.
The 2nd Respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.

This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of the offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-13-P-3871 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further stated that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
It has denied the age, occupation and income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is delay in lodging the complaint.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is high exorbitant.
On other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner prove that on 18.04.2022 at about 9.00 a.m., when he was standing on the extreme left side to cross the road on Kunigal-Nelamangala N.H.- 75 road, Narasandra, Kudur Hobli, Magadi taluk, Ramangara, at that time, driver of the Car bearing Reg.
No. KA-13-P-3871 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, caused the accident, due to which he sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, from whom and how much?
3. What order or Award?
7. In order to prove the case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents as per Ex.P1 to 12.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW.1 and he got marked 2 documents at Ex.R1 and Ex.R2 documents.
8. Heard the arguments.

9. My findings on the above issues as under:-

sentences.text:
As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.2 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 18.04.2022 at about 9.00 a.m., when he was standing on the extreme left side to cross the road on Kunigal-Nelamangala N.H.- 75 road,
Narasandra, Kudur Hobli, Magadi taluk, Ramangara,

at that time, driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.
KA-13-P-3871 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, caused the accident, due to which he sustained grievous injuries.

It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the offending vehicle driver and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Contending the above facts, the petitioners prayed to grant for compensation with interest and cost.

11. In order to substantiate the contentions petitioner stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, spot mahazar, IMV Report, wound certificate and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.

P6. On the other hand, respondent has examined its Manager-Legal Department as RW.1 and she got marked authorisation letter and insurance policy as Ex.R1 and R2.
12.
The accident occurred on 18.04.2022 at about 9 a.m and FIS was lodged on 18.04.2022 at 8.45 p.m.
The FIS was lodged by brother of the petitioner.
The wound certificate produced at Ex.P.5 reveals the history of injuries caused to the petitioner as RTA.
There are no reasons to distrust the evidence of the petitioner in this regard.
13. The contention of the respondent No.2 is that the accident has occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
In the cross examination, RW.1 has admitted that their company has not conducted investigation with regard to the said case.
He is giving evidence based on the records.
It is true that both the vehicle and other users of the road including the pedestrian are required to follow the traffic rules.

If the incident occurred in the highway, the vehicle will have right of way and the person who would like to cross the road is required to look either side of the road and only after ascertaining that there is no vehicle or traffic, should cross the road.
But, the situation in the city limits is totally different.
In the city limits, the vehicle cannot claim right off way.
The constant moving of the people in the city limits is usual and permissible.
It is true that specific zebra crossing is provided for the pedestrian to cross the road.
Normally people shall opt for it.
But in the present case, it is not the case of the respondents that zebra crossing was available near the place of occurrence.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the petitioner was prohibited from crossing the road at the place of occurrence as the place of accident is purely within the city limits.
Such being the case, it was the duty of the driver of the offending car to notice the petitioner and should have tried to avoid the accident.

14. As per Ex.P3 Spot Mahazar, the width of the road was 28 feet and there was sufficient opportunity to the driver of the car to notice the presence of petitioner and stop the vehicle or move from other side.
Still he has not avoided the accident.

As per the evidence of petitioner, he was Mahesha N.B vs Manjunath K.H on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114224512/
4 standing to cross the road.
The evidence on record is clear that driver of the car has failed to take reasonable care to protect the petitioner.
The driver of the car was expected to recognize the petitioner on the road and he should have slowed down his vehicle.
The doctrine of reasonable care imposes an obligation on the driver of the car to take care of the users of the road.

In this regard, in the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Ravi Kapur vs. State of Rajasthan ((2012) 9 SCC 284), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as here below:
"The doctrine of reasonable care imposes an obligation or a duty upon a person(for example a driver) to care for the pedestrian on the road and this duty attains a higher degree when the pedestrian happen to be children of tender years.

entities.text: Ravi Kapur vs. State of Rajasthan ((2012) 9 SCC 284)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is axiomatic to say that while driving a vehicle on a public way, there is an implicit duty cast on the drivers to see that their driving does not endanger the life of the right users of the road, may be either vehicular users or pedestrian.
They are expected to take sufficient care to avoid danger to others."
15. It is not even contended by the respondents that driver of the car applied the brake and tried to avoid the accident.
Therefore, the only inference that can be drawn that even after noticing the presence of the petitioner, by negligently driving the car hit to the petitioner without applying the brake.
This omission of driver of offending car constitutes the negligence on his part.
After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the car as per Ex.P6 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-3871.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-13-P-3871.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
17. It is the case of the petitioner that, on account of the accident he has sustained injuries.

Petitioner has relied upon Ex.P5 Wound certificate, which discloses that, there is cut lacerated wound right knee, abrasion wound over left leg, cut lacerated wound over right tempero region irregular shape and head injury and the doctor has opined that, the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Due to the injuries as mentioned in the wound certificate, it appears that petitioner might have suffered pain and sufferings.

Petitioner has also produced the Discharge Summary at Ex.P7 of V.P. Magnus hospital which discloses that, he was admitted in the said hospital from 18.04.2022 to 22.04.2022 and took conservative treatment.
Petitioner has produced the inpatient bill at Ex.P9 to the tune of Rs.46,000/-, medical bill at Ex.P10 for Rs.33,390/-, advance payment receipts at Ex.P11 and prescriptions at Ex.P12.
I have perused the bills and advance receipts.
Since, petitioner was admitted to V.P. Magnus hospital as per Ex.P7, he might have spent amount towards his medical treatment, conveyance and other incidental expenses.
Therefore, he is entitled for an amount of Rs.79,390/-(46,000+33,390) towards medical expenses.
The petitioner has not examined any doctor to prove the disability and hence, he is not entitled for compensation for loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

The Petitioner has stated that he was working as Mahesha N.B vs Manjunath K.H on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114224512/
5 agricultural coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to work.
But, petitioner has not produced any document to show his income.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner might not have worked for a period of 15 days and he might have suffered loss of income during the laid up period.

Considering the nature of injury and treatment taken by the petitioner, I deem it proper to award global compensation of Rs.1,35,000/- including the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, loss of income during the laid up period, conveyance,
attendant and other incidental expenses.
18. The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondent No.2 has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
19. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-13-P-3871.
It is not in dispute that 1 st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
As per Ex.R1 insurance policy, it was valid on the date of accident.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,35,000/- (Rupees one lakh thirty five thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the compensation amount, the entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
